landing.title: DotaDraft
landing.tagline: Draft five heroes. Get honest analysis. Fight for the win.
landing.pitch: DotaDraft is a browser strategy game built around the Dota 2 draft — pick a team, get a real evaluation of its strengths and weaknesses, then send it into Battle Mode against another player's draft or a professional lineup. No accounts, no downloads — just the draft.

draft.title: Draft five heroes
draft.text: Five rounds, five candidates each. Live synergy highlighting shows which pick fits what you already have — and which one fights it.

evaluate.title: Get an honest read
evaluate.text: Your lineup is scored on synergy, tempo, control, scaling and more, each axis ranked against ten thousand random teams so a number actually means something.

battle.title: Send it into battle
battle.text: Face another player's committed draft or a professional lineup. Win or lose, with a confidence tier — never a fake precise percentage.

about.title: How This Works
about.intro: DotaDraft isn't a full match simulator — there's no lane phase, no item builds, no player skill. It's an honest statistical model built on real match data, and it's upfront about what that can and can't tell you.
about.evaluationText: Your draft gets scored on things like synergy, tempo, control, and scaling — each axis is calibrated against real win-rate data from thousands of matches, not just a hand-picked formula.
about.battleText: Your draft faces another lineup. The outcome uses DotaDraft axes and tags — and also real OpenDota hero win rates plus how those heroes actually perform against each other, not only in-app stats.
about.ceilingText: A draft alone can't fully predict a real match — execution matters more than any stat sheet. We'd rather be honest about that uncertainty than pretend to false precision.

draft.poolHint: Choose one hero to fill your next slot

roleAssignment.heading: Assign Roles
roleAssignment.hint: Pick a position 1–5 for each hero. A gold dot marks positions this hero actually plays in real matches. Taking a position that's already used moves it off the other hero.

archetypeHint.four_plus_one: One dedicated Carry, four supporting pieces
archetypeHint.split_push: High mobility with map pressure / split identity
archetypeHint.tempo: Wants the game over early; does not scale
archetypeHint.deathball: Group fight draft — not a mobile split plan
archetypeHint.scaling: Wants the late game; soft early tempo

evaluation.radarAlt: Radar chart of this draft's percentile on each evaluation axis
evaluation.radarNote: Distance from the centre is the percentile against 10,000 random teams. The dashed ring is average.
evaluation.combosBattleNote: These combos do not change the Evaluation score above — they apply in Battle.
evaluation.combosBattleSummary: In Battle, active tags can buff or debuff your draft (and curse the opponent). Treat them as part of the fight, not this score.

commitToPool.done: Committed to the Opponent Pool — other players may now face this draft in Battle Mode.

battle.title: Battle Mode
battle.screenIntro: Send this draft against another player's or a professional lineup. Battle uses DotaDraft axes and tags — and real OpenDota win rates plus how those heroes perform against each other, not only in-app stats.
battle.shutdownBlurb: The hero underperforms their own average against every hero on the opposing draft.
battle.shutdownNoteMine: Your {{hero}} is in Shutdown: underperforms their own average against every hero on the opposing draft (−10% power).
battle.shutdownNoteOpponent: Opponent’s {{hero}} is in Shutdown: underperforms their own average against every hero on your draft (−10% power).
battle.realWinRateNote: Win rates from real games (OpenDota) — hero's overall → into this opponent.
battle.explanationBlurb: Why this matchup resolved this way — lanes, pairs, axes, tags, and the carry late from this fight. Not a reconstructed replay.

story.title: How the match may have unfolded
story.disclaimer: A read from this fight's lanes, pairs, and axes — not a reconstructed replay.
story.turnerLine: {{turner}} is the one who turns a lost fight — the save, not the first jump in.
story.openingLaneHook: It actually breaks in the {{openingLane}}: {{openingPairHero}} into {{openingPairVs}} ({{openingPairWinRate}}%) is a real hole, not just a lane score.
story.carryLateMatchup: Late, the argument is {{myCarry}} vs {{theirCarry}} — {{lateMatchupWinner}} owns that matchup ({{carryWinRate}}%).
story.carryScale: The longer this lives, the more dangerous {{scaleLeader}} gets.
story.openingAhead: {{winner}} takes the lanes {{winnerLanes}}–{{loserLanes}}. {{driver}} is first into every fight — that's whose tempo the opening is on.
story.openingComeback: The lanes went {{loserLanes}}–{{winnerLanes}} against the side that still wins. {{driver}} is the one who has to drag the map back.
story.openingEven: Nobody takes the lanes clean. From here it's fights, and {{driver}} is the one who starts them.
story.openingUpset: The favorite closed the lanes {{winnerLanes}}–{{loserLanes}}. If this flips, it starts with who walks into the fights first: {{driver}}.
story.turningCatchCombo: {{posture}}{{matchupWinner}} gets onto {{matchupLoser}} ({{matchupWinRate}}%). {{comboA}} + {{comboB}} ({{comboWinRate}}%) is the pairing that actually wins games together — that's the turn.
story.turningCatch: {{posture}}{{matchupWinner}} gets onto {{matchupLoser}} ({{matchupWinRate}}%). That's the matchup the other side doesn't solve while it's on the map.
story.turningCombo: {{posture}}{{comboA}} + {{comboB}} ({{comboWinRate}}%) is not a vibe. Together they win games, and the turn is tied to that pair.
story.turningAxis: {{posture}}There's no pretty catch on the sheet. The winning side's real edge is {{topAxis}} — the thing the other draft doesn't answer.
story.turningUpsetHighSkill: {{swingHero}} is the kind of hero who steals games the sheet can't price. This one went the wrong way for the favorite.
story.conversionRoshanEarly: This is a tempo draft. The game they want ends in the {{roshanBand}} window — after that, they're playing against the other roster's late game.
story.conversionRoshanMid: Neither side has a sharp clock. The fight lives in the {{roshanBand}} window, where Roshan is the prize if someone can actually take the map.
story.conversionRoshanLate: This draft is playing for the {{roshanBand}} window. If the game gets there, the late game is the actual win condition.
story.finishHeld: The pre-fight read held. This was their game if they didn't give the clock away.
story.finishComeback: The lanes lied about the ending. They didn't win the lane phase — they won the game anyway.
story.finishUpset: The underdog closed it. The pre-fight favorite was supposed to be the story. They weren't.

tapalka.heading: Waiting Room
tapalka.tiFormNote: Win leaders from {{count}} matches in the current TI snapshot. Ranked by wins, with win rate as the tie-breaker.

legend.title: Legend
legend.rolesNote: Portrait border/tint colors show a hero's real position, from actual match data — not the role you assign them.
legend.pickHighlightBest: Best real synergy with your picks so far, among this round's 5 candidates
legend.pickHighlightWorst: Worst real synergy with your picks so far, among this round's 5 candidates
legend.tagsNote: Hand-authored combo tags — hover a badge to see what it does. Border color shows rarity.
legend.percentileNote: How this draft's score on an axis ranks against 10,000 random 5-hero teams.

leaderboard.title: Leaderboard
leaderboard.runsNote: Your best single-session drafts, ranked by wins and win rate across the battles you fought with them.
leaderboard.runsEmpty: No runs yet — draft a team and fight at least 5 battles with it in one session to make the board.
leaderboard.note: Ranks committed drafts by how they perform as the opponent in other players' battles — not your own personal win/loss record.
leaderboard.empty: No drafts have been fought yet — commit one to the pool and start battling.
